Dead ends and gaps:
1) dominord.com/rules (Domino RD app) sits behind a Cloudflare JavaScript and cookie challenge. It returned 403 and I did not try to get around it. A search snippet credited to it or a similar site said, in parejas, each pair's total is compared, but I could not verify this.
2) comojugardomino.com/es/blog/domino-dominicano returned 502 on every try.
3) elcaribe.com.do 'Ley del dominó' returned 403, and the Wayback Machine has no copy (its index was also temporarily offline). FichaFlow cites this Dominican newspaper for a 25-point capicúa.
4) The live dr1.com article returns only the text 'conn'. I read the 2015 Wayback copies of both pages (dominoes.shtml and dominoes_1.shtml).
5) jugueton.com.do redirects to a login page. msmorell.com (Dominican vocabulary) failed with an SSL error. The Biblioteca Nacional Pedro Henríquez Ureña catalog (403) lists a Dominican book I could not read: 'El juego de domino: práctica, teoría y reglamentos, además los juegos: pintintin, la americana, combiniche'.
6) The session hit the web search cap (200) before I could run searches on Dominican use of 'pollona' and 'dar agua'. No Dominican source I opened defines 'dar agua'. Wikipedia's Dominican section only says a player of the losing team shuffles.
7) Listín Diario, Hoy, El Nuevo Diario, El Día, and N Digital produced no rules explainer. Their domino pieces use capicúa and tranque as metaphors, or report results; the 2019 Bávaro tournament winner was a team named 'Capicúa 25'.

Findings on the owner's specific points:
- Capicúa with a double (ends 2 and 2, last tile the 2-2): every source I opened says it does NOT count. Dominican sources: the Wikipedia Dominican section, DR1 (also excludes a blank), dominoarteociencia's DR note, Our Pastimes, and FichaFlow. Non-Dominican sources agree: Puerto Rico (pagat 'dominao', caribbeantrading) and eastern Cuba. The only contrary text was a search-engine summary line ('if the ends match, it must be the matching double'). I could not trace it to a page, and the fetched FichaFlow page says the opposite.
- Dominican sources give capicúa as 25 (DR1, Santiago 2019) or 30 (La Guáyiga 2025), '25 o 30' (Wikipedia), or 'vale doble' in some groups (Diario Libre).
- Pass bonuses and the target: I found NO source that says a pass bonus cannot win the game, or that a bonus stops counting when it would reach the target. I also found none that says the game can only be won by winning a hand. Sources only say the game ends when a pair 'alcanza o supera' 100 or 200. The 'both sides pass the target in one hand' case appears only in generic (non-Dominican) variants where both pairs score their own points after a lock (Kapiku, pagat).
- Tranque 'con el de abajo' (the blocker against the player on his right) is well supported: DR1, the Wikipedia patio rule, La Guáyiga 2025, Santiago 2019 rule 6. Santiago rule 12 contradicts rule 6 by saying pair against pair. Every source that states the comparison compares points (pips/tantos), not the number of tiles. Tile count appears only as an international tie-break. Tie outcomes differ: the opener wins (DR1, Wikipedia regla general), nobody scores and the lead rotates (Santiago), or the blocker wins (FichaFlow).
- 1v1: Wikipedia says 7 each with drawing from the pile, or a 10-each no-draw variant; FichaFlow says 7 each with a boneyard. No source says whether the pass bonuses apply in 1v1.
- La Guáyiga lists 'Paso corrido: +30 pts al equipo contrario' among its penalties. This is ambiguous: it may mean the team opposite the players who passed.
- DR1 gives the pase de salida as 10 points in games to 200 or 250, and 25 in games to 500. Santiago 2019 gives it as 25.

FEDERATION PICTURE: I found no published rulebook from the Federación Dominicana de Dominó Inc. (Fededodo, president Ing. Robinson Parra, reelected for 2024-2028; sources: elnuevodiario.com.do 2020, Diario Libre 2025). Fededodo sends the national team to the FEMUNDO world championship. I read the full FEMUNDO 2025 rulebook, linked from femundo.org/reglamento.html, and the FID rulebooks (2015 via pagat.com, 2024 via fidomino.org). None of them has capicúa, pase de salida, or pase corrido bonuses. In all three, a hand is scored only by the tiles left, and a match is won only by hand points reaching the target (200). FID and FEMUNDO both count all unplayed tiles, including the winner's partner. Tranques are pair against pair, and a tie scores nothing and rotates the opener. The first opener is drawn by lot and later openers rotate to the right. The FID 2015 rulebook lists Dominican delegates (Alberto Ramírez, Manuel Tejada (RD)) among its drafters.

The bonuses (capicúa 25/30, pase de salida 10/25/30, pase corrido 25/30) appear only in informal/patio sources and in municipal Dominican tournaments: Santiago 2019 and La Guáyiga 2025. The Santiago rules contradict themselves on the tranque: rule 6 says "con el de abajo" and rule 12 says "con todos, pareja con pareja".

CAPICÚA AND DOUBLES (the user's 2-2 example): every Dominican source that mentions doubles excludes them. These are Wikipedia es (Dominican section), DR1 2007 (which also excludes a blank), dominoarteociencia, and ourpastimes. In Puerto Rico, a double that fits both ends is called "Dominao" and gets no capicú bonus. Only Boarden's generic definition leaves doubles out of the question. FichaFlow also excludes a non-double such as 5-6 on ends 5 and 5, while the Wikipedia wording ("puede ser colocada por ambos extremos") would include it. I found no Dominican source that counts a double as capicúa.

PASS BONUS VS TARGET: I found no Dominican source that says whether pass bonuses can take a team past the target. Only the Boarden app states that bonuses are capped and that a hand must be won. FID and FEMUNDO have no bonuses, so the question does not arise in federation play.

Scope: apps and online games, plus the Dominican media and tournament pages those apps cite. I excluded github.com/aaguasvivas/capi (the owner's own app) wherever it appeared in results.

Sources I could not open or read in full:
- dominord.com/rules (Domino RD web game): Cloudflare bot challenge. I did not bypass it, and it has no Wayback copy. Search snippets say it has "modo informal" rules: capicúa as a last tile playable on either end, pase de salida normally 25, and a pair-total tranque. I could not quote the original, so I made no claim from it.
- elcaribe.com.do "Ley del dominó" (2012 Dominican newspaper, the 25-point capicúa source FichaFlow cites): 403 Cloudflare, no archive copy.
- comojugardomino.com Dominican article: HTTP 502 on every attempt, no archive copy.
- DR1 dominoes article: the live URL returns only "conn". I read both pages from Wayback snapshots (2022-10-14 and 2024-07-08).
- Blocked or broken: mundijuegos rules (503), dominoesonline.com (DNS failure), kapiku.com (certificate error; the wixsite copy I read is generic and not Dominican), and the Medium domino-dev article (403).
- WebFetch could not load Apple and Google Play pages (429 or truncated). I read the listings with curl instead.
- The web search budget ran out partway through (200 searches, shared with the session), so I did not run searches on "dar agua", "chuchazo con la caja" or "la primera". I found no source for "dar agua" as a shuffle term; La Mesa uses "lavar".
- I did not read the FID regulation PDF that FichaFlow links (fidomino.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Reglamento-FID-NEW-2024.pdf), or any Federación Dominicana de Dominó page. They fall under the federation lane.

Conflicts to pass on:
1. Capicúa with a double on matching ends (the owner's 2-and-2 example): only La Mesa counts it (its example: ends 6 and 6, last tile 6-6). An older search snippet of FichaFlow said the same, but the live page, updated today, excludes it. Wikipedia's DR patio section, DR1, dominoarteociencia and FichaFlow all say a double is not capicúa. DR1 adds that a capicúa made "with a blank" is also void. In Puerto Rico (Mesa28), a double closing both ends has its own name, "dominau", and pays no bonus.
2. Tranque comparison: Wikipedia (patio), DR1 ("tranquar con el de abajo"), La Guáyiga 2025, Santiago 2019 rule 6 and FichaFlow all compare the blocker with the next player, on his right. Wikipedia's Regla General, La Mesa, Boarden, Tranca and Santiago rule 12 compare team totals. The tie rule also differs by source: the opener or the opening pair wins (DR1, Wikipedia, La Mesa), the blocker wins (FichaFlow), or no points (Boarden, Tranca, Santiago, FID).
3. Direction: DR1, Wikipedia ("a la derecha"), FichaFlow, OurPastimes and the DR1 forum all say counter-clockwise, to the right. La Mesa says clockwise, and the Tranca code comment says "clockwise: the seat to your right", which mislabels the same thing.
4. Bonus amounts: pase de salida is 10 in games to 200/250 and 25 in games to 500 (DR1), 25 or 30 (Wikipedia), 25 (Santiago, FichaFlow), 10 (Boarden), or 30 (a user review of República dominó). Paso corrido is 25 (DR1), 25 or 30 (Wikipedia), 0 (Santiago), or +30 "al equipo contrario" (La Guáyiga, ambiguous wording).
5. Can bonuses win the game? Only Boarden says so explicitly: bonuses are capped and a team must win a hand to cross the target. No Dominican media or tournament source I found addresses it. La Mesa says only "the first pair to cross the total wins". Winning mid-hand appears only in Puerto Rico's Ponce variant.
6. Which hands count when a player goes out: only the opponents (DR1 for 200 games, Wikipedia Regla General, Acento, Tranca) versus all four hands (DR1 for 500 games, Wikipedia patio, La Mesa, FichaFlow tranque, Santiago tournament).
7. 1v1: Wikipedia (7 each and draw from the pile, or a variant with 10 each and no drawing) and FichaFlow (7 each with a boneyard). FichaFlow says paso redondo does not exist at a two-player table.

FichaFlow contradicts itself across pages. One page says the blocker is compared with the next player and all four hands count; another describes team totals. I reported each page as written.

No official FEDOMDOM (Dominican federation) rulebook turned up online. jugardominoenlinea.com/torneos.html says the Copa FEDOMDOM uses double-nine tiles and a 'pollona' penalty. That contradicts every other Dominican source (double-six). The page reads like generated content, so I left it out of the claims. A search snippet from the same site mentioned double-six with a 'parcel system'.

Findings on the owner's points:
(1) Capicúa with a double. Every source that addresses doubles excludes them from capicúa: es.wikipedia RD section, dominoarteociencia (RD), the DR1 article (which also cancels a finish made with a blank), the DR1 1999 forum post, FichaFlow, all Puerto Rican sources, and pagat. So "ends 2 and 2, go out with the 2-2" is not capicúa in any source I could read. The only wording that could support the owner's idea is Cuban: "misma cifra por ambos extremos" (visitcubago). One search-engine snippet of unclear origin said "if the ends match, it must be the matching double". I could not find that text on any page, and FichaFlow's current page says the opposite.
(2) Pass bonus that would reach the target. No source says a pass bonus cannot take a team to or past the target. Wikipedia RD and FID say the match ends when a pair "alcanza o supera" the target, or reaches it first, and they give no exception. The owner's rule (you can only win by winning the hand) has no written source I could find. The shared search budget ran out (200/200) before a targeted search on this point. Treat it as a house rule the owner confirms.
(3) Tranque against the player to the right. This is well sourced for Dominican play: Wikipedia patio mode, the DR1 article ("tranquar con el de abajo"), the Santiago 2019 and La Guáyiga 2025 municipal tournaments, and ourpastimes. Regla general, FID, and the USA Domino Federation compare pair against pair instead. The Santiago rules list both (rules 6 and 12 contradict each other). All sources compare points (pips/tantos), never the number of tiles.
(4) Tie on tranque. Sources differ: the pair that opened wins (Wikipedia regla general), no points and the next player opens (Santiago, FID, USA Fed), or the tie goes to the blocker (FichaFlow).
(5) Tranque points. Sources differ: the opponents' hands only (Wikipedia regla general), or all four hands (FID, patio, Santiago, FichaFlow).
(6) Pase de salida. It is cancelled when the opener's partner also passes (Wikipedia, DR1 article, DR1 1999 post). Amounts: 25/30 (Wikipedia), 10 or 25 depending on the target (DR1 article), 25 (Santiago). Paso corrido: 25/30 (Wikipedia), 25 (DR1), 30 (La Guáyiga), 0 (Santiago). No source found for 1v1 pass bonuses, except FichaFlow saying paso redondo does not exist in 1v1.
(7) 1v1. Wikipedia RD: 7 each with drawing from the pila, or a variant with 10 each and no drawing. For who opens in 1v1 without a 6-6, no Dominican-specific source; non-Dominican sources say the highest double opens.

My own reasoning, not from a source: with all 28 tiles dealt, a lock can only happen when both ends show the same number and all seven tiles of that number are on the table. This matches the FID Art. 56 definition. Not used: the owner's own GitHub repo (aaguasvivas/capi) appeared in search results and I did not use it as a source. This research subagent did not run the task-observer protocol, because the task was web-only.

Findings on the contested points:
- Capicua with a double. Most sources say a double does not count: Spanish Wikipedia's Dominican section, DR1 (a blank or a double cancels it), Domino Arte o Ciencia, FichaFlow, and the Puerto Rican and pagat sources (which call it "dominao", with no bonus). Two Dominican dictionary-style definitions do not exclude doubles: Acento/Roberto Guzmán ("cabeza de dos extremos") and ASALE. Only an old FichaFlow search snippet supported the owner's view, and the live page now says the opposite.
- Capicua value is 25 or 30 (El Día "Capicúa, 25"; Santiago 25; La Guáyiga 30). Wikipedia limits capicua to the informal/patio game.
- Tranque against the player to the right ("con el de abajo") appears in DR1, Wikipedia (patio), La Guáyiga 2025 and Santiago 2019 rule 6. Pair against pair appears in Wikipedia (regla general) and Santiago rule 12, which contradicts rule 6 in the same list.
- The comparison is always by points (pips/tantos), never by number of tiles. Tile count only breaks ties in the Mexican rules.
- Tie rules differ: the opener wins (Wikipedia regla general, DR1), no points (Santiago, USA Federation, FID), or the blocker wins (FichaFlow).
- Pass bonuses: paso corrido is 25/30 (Wikipedia patio, DR1 25, La Guáyiga 30) but is worth nothing in Santiago. Pase de salida is 25/30 (Wikipedia), 10 or 25 by target (DR1), or 25 (Santiago). It is cancelled if the opener's partner also passes (Wikipedia, DR1).
- La Guáyiga words the paso corrido as "+30 pts al equipo contrario", which is ambiguous about which team receives it.
- No Dominican source says whether pass bonuses can win the game or are capped at the target. Only the Boarden app caps them. The Cuban "no caben" rule (points over the target do not count) is optional and Cuban.
- Both teams passing the target in one hand only happens in variants where each team scores its own tiles in a lock (pagat, Kapiku). Those are not Dominican.
- Not found: any source for "dar agua"; any Dominican source on who opens 1v1 without the 6-6 (the Puerto Rican rule is the highest double); any Dominican rounding rule.
- FichaFlow is inconsistent across its own pages (opponents-only vs all-four-hands scoring; clockwise vs to-the-right rotation).

I skipped the task-observer session protocol because the task said not to use local files.
